dct_description_sm: This multi-year project was designed (as part of a larger initiative) to assess climate change impacts on sea ice and its interactions with coastal/estuary ice, as well as the risks that these interactions will generate for marine infrastructures. The main objectives of this project were: -To use traditional knowledge and current community observations to characterize the region's history in terms of climate change, ice, major climatic events, and effects on marine infrastructure; and  -To use a surveillance type camera technology to characterize present ice conditions and future extreme climatic events and their effects on selected maritime infrastructure sites. - To use radar satellite remote sensing to produce ice maps in the vicinity of the marine infrastructures every 3-4 days during freeze-up and break-up.    In its first year, the project focused on developing and setting up the data acquisition methodology. The second year focused on data processing. The third year on data analysis. Data will be used in conjunction with models to foresee future conditions and plan maintenance strategies for marine infrastructures.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Adaptation
dct_title_s: Study of the Behaviour of Sea and Freshwater Ice in the Vicinity of Nunavik Maritime Infrastructure - Contribution of Local Knowledge and Remote Sensing
